text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Palestinian and Israeli delegations held a meeting in Cairo and will meet again within days. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's political adviser Osama el-Baz says the talks have achieved some progress. A member of the Israeli delegation describes them as constructive.
- Mubarak to give the go-ahead signal within days to start the thrid stage of Mubarak's youth housing project.
- New expansions at Qarun oil field in the western desert to be open within the coming few days. The expansions quadrupled production to 40,000 barrels per day.

- Forty leaders of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), including four lawyers, were rounded up for trying to revive the group's activities by organising a new terrorist group. The new group planned to carry out criminal operations against important figures and senior security officers.
- Mubarak issued two decisions ending the legislative session of the parliament's two councils.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali says committees will be formed to settle disputes arising from the enforcement of a new law that ends perpetual leases of farm lands.
- Pension increases will cost the treasury 644 million pounds ($189.7 million).
